This addresses the H05 prediction of donor-linked substrate or intermediate association without presuming catalytic relevance.","evidence_ids":["EV029","GX011","EV031","EV061","EV021","EV080","GX008"],"source_to_proposal":"Sources report or interpret TEOA as capable of CO2 trapping or catalyst-adduct chemistry in non-cobalt systems and show that medium can alter observable intermediates; this proposal transfers only the testable prediction that donor identity may change observable CO2-associated states under matched Co-bpy conditions. on-pathway relevance or exact structure"] ,"supports":"Support for H05 would be reproducible CO2-dependent signatures that differ between TEA and TEOA under otherwise matched P01 conditions, especially if TEOA shows additional or stronger features absent in inert controls and not reproduced by the no-amine CO2 sample. Stronger support would come from consistent assignment logic across two observables, such as IR plus NMR, while still remaining descriptive rather than mechanistic proof.","refutes":"H05 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give no reproducible difference in any CO2-dependent pre-illumination signature under matched conditions, or if all apparent donor differences disappear after background subtraction, replicate preparation, and gas-control checks. It is also weakened if observed features are equally present under inert gas, indicating donor/background rather than CO2-associated origin.","inconclusive":"Results are inconclusive if signals are too weak, unresolved, or irreproducible; if TEA and TEOA differ but only alongside uncontrolled pH, water-content, or solubility changes; or if spectra show donor-dependent bulk amine-CO2 speciation but cannot separate that from catalyst-associated adducts. A null result does not exclude transient light-induced differences.","parameter_selection":"Do not invent concentrations or acquisition settings. Use the verified P01 baseline composition from supplied evidence. Run a short pilot to set gas-equilibration time, sample concentration window, and spectral averaging so that major solvent and donor backgrounds are stable and not detector-saturating. If both IR and NMR are attempted, choose the method giving reproducible CO2-minus-inert difference signals first; add the second method only if it offers independent assignment value. If signal overlap prevents interpretation, prioritize isotopic or background controls only after basic detectability is confirmed.","limitations":"This experiment is characterization only and cannot establish that any detected species lies on the catalytic pathway or controls CO/H2 selectivity. TEA/TEOA change multiple chemical properties beyond simple donor strength, so donor identity is a bundled factor even in the single-factor contrast. Because cobalt, bpy, and g-C3N4 remain present in all main groups, any observed signal may arise from bulk amine-CO2 chemistry, catalyst-linked adducts, support-associated species, or combinations thereof. Pre-illumination measurements may miss the operating photochemical state.","feasibility":"moderate"}]}
